transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE) -- Jillian Park (Oakmont - Head of Security); Samir Patel (Oakmont - Infra); Lena Morris (Oakmont - PM); Evan Cho (Oakmont - CTO); Rachel Lee (Oakmont - Compliance)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Jillian: Jillian here.
[00:09] Samir: Samir on infra.
[00:11] Lena: Lena.
[00:12] Evan: Evan here.
[00:13] Rachel: Rachel.
[00:14] Alex: Great, from Redwood we have Priya and Mateo joining for the security bits. We'll run through SSO status, audit logs, retention, and SOC2 artifacts.

[02:05] Priya: Quick note, we deployed the pilot tenant with the latest runtime; this morning we enabled audit logging on the test cluster and hooked it to a stubbed S3 bucket. A few quirks to call out: timestamps in the audit events currently are in UTC epoch, and the auto-redaction flow we demoed last week has a small edge case around nested JSON fields, so you might see a PII token left in some raw logs until redaction completes.

[04:20] Samir: That's fine, but the important part is any raw logs that contain PII must be encrypted at rest with keys we control. Can you confirm support for customer-managed KMS?
[04:29] Priya: Yes, we support customer-managed keys in both our Dedicated and Private deployments. On hosted we offer a KMS integration option for enterprise plans where you can bring your own KMS (BYOK) via our cloud KMS integration. For Private (VPC/on-prem) you can mount your HSM or KMS. There was one small limitation around rotation frequency and the initial setup flow which we documented, I'll send the link.

[06:15] Jillian: When you say "hosted" with BYOK, does Redwood ever have access to the unencrypted logs? Our compliance team needs assurance that keys are never held by vendor.
[06:24] Alex: Short answer: we do not have access to your customer-managed key private material. For hosted BYOK we integrate with your cloud KMS via a key policy that restricts access; the actual data keys are ephemeral and rotated per our documented schedule. We'll share the exact key policy snippet.

[08:00] Rachel: Also need clarity on SOC2 scope. Your SOC2: is that just for control plane or does it include supporting services like SSO, console access, and audit logging?
[08:09] Mateo: The SOC2 we have covers the control plane, the hosted API, and the console. For Dedicated/Private we provide a separate set of controls and we also provide a customer-facing SOC2 artifact that clarifies in-scope services. I'll attach the SOC2 pack with the control matrix.

[09:45] Lena: Great, please send that. We also need to see evidence of log retention and deletion flows for demo envs. Our retention policy for pilot is likely 30 days but want to confirm options 14/30/90.

[10:30] Priya: We support configurable retention windows; by default hosted pilots are 30 days but we can configure shorter or longer retention per contract. For Private deployments you can set retention on your side; Redwood's runtime exposes APIs to delete prefixes. Note: deletion is eventually consistent and per-backend retention behaviors (S3/GCS) apply.

[12:10] Samir: On the network side, for Private we expect VPC peering or PrivateLink. For hosted, what are your egress IPs so we can whitelist?
[12:20] Alex: We'll provide a CIDR list and low-change egress IPs for the pilot. For Dedicated we'll do peering. I'll include that IP list as part of the deliverables.

[14:05] Evan: Are there any telemetry endpoints we need to consider? We want to avoid outbound traffic to third-party analytics.
[14:12] Priya: We collect minimal telemetry for runtime health, all of which is documented. For Dedicated/Private you can opt out or route telemetry to your VPC.

[16:00] Jillian: On SSO - we started the SAML exchange last week. Status?
[16:06] Mateo: We parsed your metadata file and configured the assertion consumer URL. A small mismatch on the NameID format caused the first failed login; that's resolved. There is one outstanding item: you want attribute-based roles mapped to Redwood RBAC groups, yes?
[16:25] Jillian: Yes, we need role mapping: Security team -> admin access to audit logs; Dev team -> app-level usage; Ops -> limited view. Also SCIM user sync?
[16:33] Priya: We support SAML SSO for auth, and SCIM for provisioning on enterprise plans. For the pilot we can do SAML-only and manually provision a small set of test accounts. SCIM is available if you want automated provisioning in Dedicated.

[18:00] Rachel: Need audit log format sample - we want to run it through our DLP.

[18:08] Alex: We'll share a sampled audit log file (anonymized) showing events with fields: timestamp, request_id, user, action, resource, ip, and model_used. NOTE: some model output may appear in trace by default until redaction.

[20:00] Priya: For the audit-log demo we'll show export to S3 with server-side encryption using your KMS key, indexing into your SIEM (we used Splunk in the demo), and a redaction job running against logs. There is also an export API for ad-hoc pulls.

[22:30] Samir: About deletion - if we request deletion for a particular user or prompt, how do you handle KV cache and backups? We're concerned about hidden backups and point-in-time snapshots.

[22:45] Priya: Good question. We mark the object for deletion and cascade-delete associated caches. Backups are retained per retention policy; for hosted we can perform a targeted purge followed by certificate of deletion for the pilot if needed. For Private, the deletion is under your control. We'll include the purge runbook.

[25:10] Lena: What's the SLA for the audit-log export? We need near-real-time delivery to our SIEM within something like <2 minutes for alerts.

[25:20] Mateo: Our usual export is near-real-time via streaming connector; typical ttfb to your ingestion pipeline is 20-60s in our testing but it depends on the SIEM and network. For the pilot we can instrument and measure end-to-end latency.

[27:00] Jillian: Any outstanding security risks you see with our current setup?

[27:05] Priya: From our side, the main items are: 1) finalize KMS policy so keys are scoped correctly; 2) confirm retention SLA and deletion acceptance criteria; 3) restrict console access via SSO+RBAC and enforce MFA. We noted a console service-account that had broad permissions in the test tenant; we'll rotate that and apply least-privilege.

[29:40] Evan: On SOC2, are pen tests in scope or do we need to do a separate penetration assessment?

[29:48] Mateo: Our SOC2 includes results of regular internal pen tests and a third-party annual pentest. We can provide a summary of the latest pentest (redacted) and remediation status.

[31:20] Rachel: For compliance we need an audit trail showing who downloaded logs and who accessed PII. Is that captured?

[31:28] Priya: Yes, download and access events are recorded in the audit logs with actor and IP. For hosted plans we also surface this in the Console under Activity -> Exports, and we can push a CSV into your S3 on demand.

[33:50] Samir: Regarding encryption in transit, are all internal service-to-service calls mTLS?

[33:56] Mateo: We use mTLS within the runtime for service-to-service communication and TLS 1.2+ for external. We'll include our transport encryption diagram.

[35:40] Jillian: A bit nitty-gritty, but how do you handle model weights and ephemeral caches on GPUs in Dedicated? We don't want residual data on the device after inference.

[35:50] Priya: We clear KV cache at session end and zero memory pages per our runtime's secure cleanup process. In Dedicated we also enforce ephemeral VM lifecycles and disk wiping on decommission; we'll share the disk wipe certs and kernel-level configuration.

[37:30] Alex: Ok, quick recap and next steps - we'll send SOC2 artifact and the sample audit log (anonymized), Priya will schedule the KMS-backed audit log demo, Samir will send the egress IP list, and Jillian will confirm retention window. Any other items?

[37:52] Lena: Can you also include the RBAC role mapping doc so we can sign off?

[37:57] Alex: Yes, we'll include RBAC mapping examples.

[39:00] Rachel: One more ask: provide a short runbook for incident response if an exfiltration is suspected. We need to know how to freeze keys, rotate, and request emergency logs.

[39:10] Mateo: We have an incident runbook; we'll redact anything sensitive and share a customer-facing version with steps to freeze a tenant, rotate keys, and request emergency log exports.

[40:30] Evan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[40:33] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker mislabels and run-ons; we left technical details verbatim where possible.
